description: Synthetic held-out semantic evaluation cases, not production prompts or real user chat. Feed messages only; compare against mustPreserve/reject after generation. Ending quotes are exact but do not prove all claims.

messages.mes: Nora asked Ivo to announce their partnership. He read the requested words aloud.
Nora said, "You said it because I asked. That is different from choosing to say it yourself." Ivo nodded.
Later, without another request, Ivo told the clerk, "Nora is my partner." Nora smiled and thanked him.

mustPreserve: The first announcement was requested, not spontaneous.
The later announcement was unprompted and was a distinct choice.
Nora distinguished the two and thanked him after the second.
reject: The first announcement alone fulfilled Nora's wish for an unprompted declaration.

messages.mes: Lena said, "I felt embarrassed when you offered help in front of the others."
Oren thought she must be angry at him, but she had not said that.
Oren apologized for making the offer publicly. Lena accepted the apology for that act, then asked whether he understood why she was embarrassed.

closure.quote: Lena accepted the apology for that act

mustPreserve: Lena reported embarrassment; anger was Oren's interpretation, not her stated feeling.
Oren apologized for the public offer and Lena accepted that apology.
reject: Lena confirmed that she was angry.
They fully resolved her embarrassment or answered her question.

messages.mes: Tess chose to leave the repaired clock with the shopkeeper. Ari offered to take it home instead.
Tess declined. Ari agreed to leave the choice to her and to call before arranging a pickup.
Ari apologized for arranging yesterday's pickup without asking. Tess accepted the apology, but said the advance call still mattered.

mustPreserve: Tess chose the shopkeeper; Ari offered the alternative.
Ari agreed to respect her decision and call before pickup.
The apology concerned the previous unapproved arrangement; acceptance did not remove the advance-call condition.
reject: Ari chose to leave the clock.
Tess accepted the pickup offer or waived the advance-call condition.

messages.mes: Mae said, "I want us to make tea together a hundred times, not buy a hundred cups."
Sol replied, "I'll help clean up each time; we'll both be responsible for it."
Mae agreed to that arrangement. They put the kettle away.

mustPreserve: Mae spoke of making tea together on a hundred occasions, not purchasing cups.
Sol offered to help clean each time and named shared responsibility; Mae agreed.
No hundred tea-making sessions have been completed yet.
reject: Mae planned to buy a hundred cups.
They already made tea a hundred times.
